subject: QBR: kernel routing, batching/caching sensitivity and runway ask
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: QBR: kernel routing, batching/caching sensitivity and runway ask

Team —

QBR prep note: I want a focused readout on how kernel routing (i.e., routing requests to quantized vs fp16 kernels), batching windows, and prefix/KV caching are affecting our runway projections for H1. Specifically we need to surface:

- Current GPU spend projection for Q1 under the baseline (no additional optimizations) and two levers: aggressive batching (30% higher average batch size) and 80% KV-cache hit for common prefixes.
- Expected impact on 95/99 tail latencies for chat workloads when routing to quantized kernels vs fp16 for the medium-length seqs (256–1024 tokens).
- A short sensitivity table showing utilization and unit-cost per effective token for the three scenarios.

Asks:
1) Karthik — can you paste the consolidated slot utilization and per-GPU effective token cost for baseline / batching / caching by EOD Thu? Put the numbers into the attached qbr-runway-sheet-v3.xlsx.
2) Marissa & Jonas — please prepare one slide (bullet + chart) on the experiments that produced the batching-impact-figs.pdf and indicate confidence (low/med/high) and whether the results generalize across small/medium/large models.
3) Lauren — we'll need a brief exec-friendly summary (3 bullets) of the tradeoffs to include in the QBR deck.

For context, I attached the working sheet and the latest sim outputs (kernel-routing-sim-results.csv). There is also a Drive folder with the simulation notebooks and the HubSpot ticket linking this to the Dedicated capacity forecast: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/fake-qbr-kernel-routing

I'll run a 30m sync Thu 10:30am PT to reconcile numbers and lock the QBR ask list. If you cannot make that time, flag below.

Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Attachments: qbr-runway-sheet-v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), kernel-routing-sim-results.csv (text/csv), batching-impact-figs.pdf (presentation)

Thanks, Irene — this framing is helpful. Quick clarifying Qs before I draft the exec bullets:

- Do we want to show both gross and net GPU spend (net = after billing credits / reserved discounts)? I think execs want net but SRE will want gross for headroom planning.
- For the tail-latency note, do we have a target SLO to reference (e.g., 95p chat < 300ms)? If yes I'll call out when a scenario risks the SLO.

I can take the wording for the tradeoffs. I’ll draft 3 concise bullets and circulate a one-paragraph version for the deck by Wed EOD.

I can join Thu 10:30am PT.

-Lauren

Irene / Lauren —

I pulled the first pass numbers into qbr-runway-sheet-v3.xlsx (tab: "scenario-v1"). Below are the headline rows (rounded):

Baseline (no change)
- avg slot utilization: 62%
- effective tokens / GPU-hour: 1.1M
- projected monthly GPU spend (net): $2.8M
- 95p tail latency (chat medium seq): 240ms

Aggressive batching (+30% avg batch)
- avg slot utilization: 77%
- effective tokens / GPU-hour: 1.38M (+25%)
- projected monthly GPU spend (net): $2.25M (-19%)
- 95p tail latency: 275ms (+35ms)

High KV-cache (80% hit on common prefixes)
- avg slot utilization: 69%
- effective tokens / GPU-hour: 1.27M (+15%)
- projected monthly GPU spend (net): $2.4M (-14%)
- 95p tail latency: 255ms (+15ms)

Notes / caveats:
- The batching numbers assume the same request mix. For latency-sensitive routes we estimate we can keep batching windows shorter and still see ~15% uplift in tokens/GPU-hour.
- Quantized kernel routing (INT8 path) reduces token compute cost by ~12%, but increases 99p latency for longer sequences due to memory pressure in the decoding kernel. We model that as a net -8% spend with a +40ms 99p impact for >1024 token tails (see kernel-routing-sim-results.csv).
- Projections above are net after expected marketplace discounts; gross spend is ~8% higher.

Action items I completed: populated scenario tab, attached kernel-routing-sim-results.csv, and added short comments on confidence levels (low/med/high). I'll update if we run a longer sim on the int8 path.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Infrastructure Economics
Redwood Inference

Great progress — thank you. Quick synthesis and final asks for the Thu sync: 

Synthesis (for exec slide):
- Conservatively, batching + cache can reduce net monthly GPU spend by ~14–19% versus baseline (mix-dependent). Expect a latency uplift concentrated at 95/99p; for our primary chat SLO (95p < 300ms) both levers remain within SLO for medium sequences.
- Quantized kernel routing offers additional spend savings (~8% net) but introduces risk to 99p for very long tails; recommend canary the int8 path for non-critical routes and measure 99p before wider rollout.
- Present both gross and net spend numbers in the deck; gross for capacity planning and net for finance/runway.

Final asks before Thu 10:30am PT sync: 
1) Karthik: add a gross spend column to scenario-v1 tab and a short note on model-mix sensitivity (EOD Thu).
2) Marissa & Jonas: add a single chart comparing 95p/99p across scenarios and annotate confidence (EOD Wed).
3) Lauren: drop me the 3 exec bullets Wed EOD so I can merge into the draft QBR deck.

I'll pull the qbr deck and fold these into the infra slide set; we will call out the fallback policy (route to fp16 when 99p crosses +50ms delta).

If anyone needs the Drive links or can't make Thu 10:30am PT, reply-all.

Thanks — Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: qbr-runway-sheet-v3.xlsx, batching-impact-figs.pdf, kernel-routing-sim-results.csv
